evidence: the-key-is-private-and-matches-the-certificate: ssl_base.pp:77-78 (with 85-92) put the non-LE key at /etc/ssl/private/<prefix>.key, mode 0600, owner/group root by default; with sslprefix p8test the probe stats /etc/ssl/private/p8test.key for root:root 600 and compares its public key with the bundle's first certificate (from <prefix>.crt, line 80). Mismatch varies the certificate compared (the issuer's), which must change the verdict, and it failed after apply

the-bundle-is-the-leaf-then-its-issuer: ssl_base.pp:109-119 concat fragments order 01 <prefix>.crt then 02 <prefix>.intermediate.crt into the bundle at line 79 (/etc/ssl/certs/p8test.nginx.bundle.crt, since ssl_nginx_domain passes myservice nginx); concat at 100-107 sets 0644 root:root. The probe checks 644 root:root, two certificates, CN p8test.invalid then the throwaway CA (the fixture's intermediate stand-in), and that the first verifies against the second. Mismatch swaps only the trust anchor to the system CA bundle, which did not sign the leaf, and it failed after apply

nginx-serves-tls-with-the-pair: ssl_base.pp:79-81 name the bundle (leaf then intermediate) and ssl_nginx_domain.pp:9-14 deliver it for the nginx service; the action (declared in mutates: one conf.d server block on 127.0.0.1:8443 naming the deployed bundle and key, plus reload) only lets nginx load the pair, and the read-only effect performs the handshake and checks nginx sends 2 certificates, leaf CN p8test.invalid, chain verifying against the second, i.e. the action's result, not its output

purpose gap: Tested on Ubuntu: key at /etc/ssl/private/p8test.key root:root 0600 matching the certificate; bundle leaf-then-intermediate root:root 0644 verifying; nginx actually serving TLS with the pair and sending the intermediate; drift reverted by the agent run with exactly one nginx restart. Honestly uncovered: RedHat private dir (rhel9, active in nodes.yml) and the Let's Encrypt fixture variant (with the nginx_frontend_mail partial coverage stated truly). Gap: the outcome 'nginx is restarted once when the key or certificate changes' and its cited ssl_base.pp:10 ('The service is restarted if the certificate changes') are probed only by drifting the key AND the bundle together, so a missing notify on either file (e.g. the concat's notify at 100-107) would still pass with one restart from the other; a certificate-only change (a renewal that keeps the key) is exercisable on this lab and is untested. Drifting the bundle alone (and/or the key alone) before an agent run would close it
